data.body_markdown: Tom and Cat spent years in mortgage banking before deciding the world needed one more genuinely good neighborhood coffee shop more than it needed two more bankers. Haddon Heights residents themselves, they opened Trouble Brewing at 514 Station Ave on **Friday the 13th of October, 2017** — about as on-brand an opening day as a shop called Trouble could ask for. It's been a warm, art-filled room where the coffee is serious and the vibe is not ever since.

data.intro: We partnered with **La Colombe** because great coffee shouldn't be complicated — it should be consistent, ethical, and delicious. That partnership is the foundation we build every drink on, alongside **Metolius** teas and breakfast served all day.

testimonials.author: Hazel Stjernelys
testimonials.quote:
While browsing for coffee shops in the area, this one caught my eye. It did not disappoint! This shop is cozy, clearly loved by locals, and has plenty of seating without feeling overcrowded. Chosen decor includes foxes and mushrooms and adds the right touch of whimsy 🍄
I'm not out this way often but I'll definitely stop again the next time I am!

testimonials.author: Cory Mathews
testimonials.quote: Good coffee for a good price. Blueberry scone was very good massive Blueberrys barista Tyler was friendly and fast would visit again when on a trip from California

testimonials.author: Leticia Vega
testimonials.quote: My son and I stopped in to have a hot chia and cold latte with breakfast sandwiches and pastries. Great service, drinks and food great. Beautiful town. Been there before. Bonus--it's dog friendly 🦮. Definitely will be back.

testimonials.author: Heather Roth
testimonials.quote: Definitely one of my favorite coffee shops that I have come across. I love that they collaborate with other local businesses. I’m a big fan of their Milky Way iced coffee, and their breakfast sandwiches are delicious. I love hanging out inside or outside. Their staff are fantastic. I love chatting with them every time I go in.

reviews.text: I love this coffee shop & I’m excited to come back and try more of the food/drinks on their menu. It was pretty busy this morning, but the staff was still very friendly and helpful. Our orders also came up pretty quickly for how busy it was! The restaurant itself is so cute - I love how it’s decorated with the gallery wall and variety of seating. Perfect place to get some work done because there is a lot of seating inside and outside with their wifi password on the wall. There’s also a free little library with some good book selections so I’ll definitely be back to exchange!!

local_businesses.name: Cabana Water Ice Co.
local_businesses.blurb: Homemade water ice and hand-dipped ice cream, going since 1989. The summer half of a Station Ave afternoon.

local_businesses.name: John's Friendly Market
local_businesses.blurb: The old-fashioned neighborhood grocery and deli. Exactly the sort of place a main street stops being a main street without.

local_businesses.name: Lula's Empanadas
local_businesses.blurb: Contemporary Dominican empanadas from Yaslyn Lora, named after her mother — up to eighteen flavors, now from a proper Station Ave storefront. They chipped in prizes for our ninth-birthday raffle.

local_businesses.name: South Jersey Special
local_businesses.blurb: Amy Murphy’s gift shop of South Jersey makers — cards, prints, jewelry and small-batch things, most of it funny, all of it local. Another of our birthday-raffle donors.

local_businesses.name: Jane's Tea House
local_businesses.blurb: Proper afternoon tea a few doors up. The one place on the street we happily send people for a hot drink.

local_businesses.name: April Robin Florist & Gift
local_businesses.blurb: The florist at the top of the avenue — where the flowers on our counter usually come from.

local_businesses.name: Anthony's Creative Italian Cuisine
local_businesses.blurb: BYOB Italian right next door, in three dining rooms inside a 1930s building. Our closest neighbor by about twenty feet.

local_businesses.name: Ralph's Pizza
local_businesses.blurb: Family-run pizza on Station Ave for more than thirty years, with a back room that has hosted half the birthdays in town. They donated to our ninth-birthday raffle, too.

timeline_events.title: Trouble opens on Station Ave
timeline_events.description: Tom and Cat, Haddon Heights locals, open Trouble Brewing Coffee House at 514 Station Ave — on Friday the 13th, naturally. La Colombe in the grinder, breakfast all day.

timeline_events.title: The internet finds out
timeline_events.description: New Jersey Isn’t Boring writes Trouble up as one of the best spots around to work from a coffee shop — comfy seats, free WiFi, a shelf of books and drinks sized Trouble and Big Trouble.

timeline_events.title: Nine years of Trouble
timeline_events.description: A birthday raffle with prizes from our Station Ave neighbors — Lula’s Empanadas, Ralph’s Pizza, South Jersey Special and Doc’s Unique Boutique — and two birthday lattes: The Max (a dirt-cake iced latte) and The Ruby (cake batter, strawberry cold foam, sprinkles).

timeline_events.title: A Quick Bites review
timeline_events.description: The Retrospect stops in for its Quick Bites column and comes away talking about the cappuccino, the pumpkin spice frozen coffee and the French toast muffin — "a group favorite."
